messages:
Alex (arch): Quick q — thinking about canary/A-B cutovers: should the runtime orchestrate drift-aware cutover (redirecting traffic based on model output drift) or should that live entirely in the control plane? tradeoffs for latency, signal freshness, and rollback safety.
Mira: +1 for discussing. what signals do we mean by 'drift'? output distribution shift? latency/error? user-behaviour? :thinking:
Samir: My vote: keep detection and heavy aggregation in telemetry/control plane but expose a lightweight 'variant health' API the runtime can query. that keeps runtime decision fast without reimplementing analytics.
Jen - runtime: runtime can either poll or accept pushes. polling => eventual consistency and tail decisions; push => needs secure channels + heartbeats. runtime must assume partial info and provide local safety knobs.
Alex (arch): Right. I'm imagining a "drift score" per variant per region (sliding window) + sample_count + p95 latency. runtime uses thresholds but control plane owns scoring. also need an escape hatch if scoring absent.
Mira: Also remember KV/prefix cache warmups: switching to a variant with cold cache will spike latency and look like the model itself regressed. we need a warmup_grace in the policy.
Samir: Suggest adding a warmup window that masks latency signals for N minutes after weight increase. also treat cold-cache latency separately in scoring.
Alex (arch): Sketch of a minimal runtime query API:
```
# runtime -> control plane
GET /v1/variant_health?model=foo&region=us-west
# response (pre-aggregated)
{"variant":"v2","score":0.92,"sample_count":1200,"latency_pct_95":180}
```
Jen - runtime: Contract notes: sample_count must be approximate and bounded; p95 should be pre-aggregated buckets. Also runtime needs deterministic fallback for session-affinity to avoid user flapping.
Mira: For A/B experiments we also need exposure quotas. routing must track separate token pools: production vs experiment exposures. fallback should respect experiment quotas (don't steal experiment traffic silently).
Samir: Yup. implement token pools and a priority rule: safety fallback < experiment quota enforcement. i.e., only fail experiment quota if safety demands it and ops approves.
Alex (arch): Draft fallback policy proto (rough):
```
fallback_policy:
  - on_error: route_to: default
  - on_drift: when: score < 0.8 and sample_count > 200 -> gradual_weight_shift: 10%/min
  - on_latency_spike: when: p95 > 500 and p95_delta > 200 -> drain_variant
```
We should also define cooldowns and max step-down per minute.
Jen - runtime: runtime safety knobs: max_step_down_per_min, cooldown_window, emergency_fallback_ttl to avoid oscillation. also need an audit log + trace id so rollback events are debuggable.
Mira: Telemetry needs to ship both pre- and post-cutover traces and a join key so we can disambiguate warmup vs regressions. include synthetic warmup probes.
Samir: Ops/SRE need alerts on ambiguous borderline scores (0.75-0.85) and a manual override in the rollout console. also provide a dry-run mode for traffic-slicing simulation.
Alex (arch): Ownership proposal: control plane owns scoring, policy authoring, and experiment quotas. runtime owns enforcement, local safety state, and emergency toggles. we need clear API contracts and SLAs for push/poll freshness.
Jen - runtime: sounds good. i'll prototype enforcement API (support push+pull) and implement safety knobs in the runtime flags. estimate: 2w prototype.
Mira: i'll produce the drift scoring recipe + signals list (one week).
Samir: i'll sketch quota separation and token-pool semantics (one week).
Alex (arch): action items for Ops: define alert thresholds and playbook for manual overrides.
Alex (arch): deploy-bot FYI: we'll want a canary rollout tomorrow for demo.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by @alex: model/foo v2 -> canary 5% us-west @ 2025-05-01T15:00Z :rocket:
Mira: noted — i'll include warmup sets and synthetic probes.
Jen - runtime: i'll add local cooldown and emergency toggle to canary flags. will share flag names.
Samir: i'll ensure experiment quotas and a fail-open policy are in place.
Alex (arch): thanks all. we'll sync next week and fold notes into a short RFC.
